statements.claim: Akrura had come to Vrindavan as Kamsa's messenger and bowed to the ground on beholding Krishna
statements.evidence: VP 5.18 (Wilson): 'I am Akrúra,' and bowed his head down to the feet of Hari; pack excerpt: Kamsa sent Akrura as messenger.

statements.claim: Krishna asked why Akrura asked after their welfare when the trouble in their own family only grows
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.4: 'kiṃ nu naḥ kuśalaṃ pṛcche edhamāne kulāmaye' (why ask of our welfare while the family affliction grows).

statements.claim: Akrura told of Kamsa's enmity toward the Yadavas, his resolve to kill Vasudeva, and that the errand was meant to draw the brothers to Mathura
statements.evidence: BP 10.39 excerpt: 'Kamsa's enmity toward the Yadavas, his resolve to kill Vasudeva, and the reason he himself had been sent as messenger'; canonical event evt_0124.

statements.claim: Akrura described Vasudeva grown old in sorrow, limbs wasted, oppressed by Kamsa of sinful designs, mind burning with anxiety
statements.evidence: HV 1.81 (Dutt): 'he has grown old and all his limbs have become lean... always oppressed by Kansa of sinful designs... mind is always burning in anxiety.'

statements.claim: Akrura described Devaki growing lean like a cow separated from her calf, sons never at her breast, eyes sunk like the moon seized by Rahu, soiled garments, parted from her sons since infancy
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'growing lean out of grief... like a cow without her calf... Like unto the moon possessed by Rāhu her eyes have run into their sockets and clad in a soiled raiment... separated from thee from thy very infancy.'

statements.claim: Akrura's sayings on sons: a woman without children bears one grief; a woman whose sons accomplish nothing knows no end of sorrow; Devaki deserves reverence as the earth does; save the goddess sunk in the water of sorrow
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'Women, having no children, are subject to one grief only... no end of their miseries, if they... have not their ends accomplished'; 'If like unto earth who holds thee Devaki deserves thy respect it behoves thee to save that goddess sunk into the water of sorrow.'

statements.claim: Akrura recalled Krishna's feats: vanquishing Kaliya in the Yamuna, lifting Govardhana, destroying Arishta and Keshi
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'as thou didst vanquish the wicked Nāga Kalya in the lake of Yamunā, as thou didst uproot the mount Govardhana... destroy the powerful Arishtha... kill the wicked-minded Keshi.'

statements.claim: Krishna knew everything, took no offence, and answered simply 'So be it'
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'The powerful Krishna knew everything so without taking any offence at the words of the liberal prince he said "So be it"' (BP-following rendering; VP variant with three-night vow noted in tradition_note).

statements.claim: The cowherds led by Nanda resolved to obey Kamsa's summons, arranged tributes of buffaloes, bulls, curd, milk and clarified butter
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'all the Gopas, headed by Nanda, desired to follow the orders of Kansa... buffaloes and bull, curd, milk and clarified butter.'

statements.claim: Akrura spent the night without sleep speaking with Krishna and Balarama; at dawn Vraja stirred and prepared to travel
statements.evidence: HV 1.81: 'Conversing with Krishna and Rohini's son Akrura spent the night without sleep'; dawn description follows.

notes: Tradition note correctly flags VP 5.18's three-night vow variant; story follows BP/HV. No issues.

statements.claim: Nanda ordered the cowherds to gather all milk products and carry tribute to Mathura the next day
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.10-11: 'gṛhyatāṃ sarva-go-rasaḥ... yāsyāmaḥ śvo madhu-purīṃ dāsyāmo nṛpate rasān'.

statements.claim: Hearing this the gopis were stricken with grief; some lost the light of their faces, others stopped all activity lost in thought of him, others remembered his smiles, gait and glances and feared separation
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.12-17: 'babhūvur vyathitā bhṛśam... śvāsa-mlāna-mukha-śriyaḥ... nivṛttāśeṣa-vṛttayaḥ... smarantyaś... gatiṃ su-lalitāṃ... snigdha-hāsāvalokanam.'

statements.claim: The gopis accused Akrura: he showed them Mukunda's face with dark curls, fair cheeks, fine nose and sorrow-dispelling smile, then took it out of their sight; called Akrura ('not cruel') he is cruel, giving them eyes then stealing what they were given to see
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.19-20: 'yas tvaṃ pradarśyāsita-kuntalāvṛtaṃ mukunda-vaktraṃ su-kapolam un-nasam śokāpanoda-smita-leśa-sundaraṃ karoṣi pārokṣyam asādhu te kṛtam'; 'krūras tvam akrūra-samākhyayā... cakṣur hi dattaṃ harase.'

statements.claim: The gopis feared the women of Mathura would enjoy Krishna's company and that he, charmed by polished city speech and bashful smiles, would never endure their rustic words
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.22-24 ('sukhaṃ prabhātā rajanī... pura-yoṣitāṃ... adya dhruvaṃ tatra dṛśo bhaviṣyate'); VP 5.18: 'he will never again endure the rustic expressions of the Gopís.'

statements.claim: The gopis said Nanda's son is new to affection and his friendship breaks in a moment; they gave up homes, kin, children and husbands to serve him
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.21: 'kṣaṇa-bhaṅga-sauhṛdaḥ... nava-priyaḥ... vihāya gehān sva-janān sutān patīṃs tad-dāsyam addhopagatā.'

statements.claim: The gopis resolved to stop Madhava, saying elders and kinsmen could do nothing; he stood dry-hearted mounting the chariot while the mad ones urged him on
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.26-27: 'anārdra-dhīr eṣa samāsthito rathaṃ tam anv amī ca tvarayanti durmadāḥ / nivārayāmaḥ samupetya mādhavaṃ kiṃ no 'kariṣyan kula-vṛddha-bāndhavāḥ.'

statements.claim: The gopis recalled Krishna returning to Vraja at day's end, dust of hooves on hair and garland, playing his flute with smiling sidelong glances, stealing their hearts
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.29: 'yo 'hnaḥ kṣaye vrajam... gopair viśan khura-rajaś-churitālaka-srak veṇuṃ kvaṇan smita-katākṣa-nirīkṣaṇena cittaṃ kṣiṇoti.'

statements.claim: His affection, smiles, sweet words, playful glances and embraces made their nights pass like a moment; without him they could not cross the darkness ahead
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.28: 'nītāḥ sma naḥ kṣaṇam iva kṣaṇadā vinā taṃ gopyaḥ kathaṃ nv atitarema tamo durantam.'

statements.claim: They wept with bracelets loose upon their wasted arms and grieved through the night
statements.evidence: VP 5.18: 'they wept bitterly, their bracelets were loose upon their arms'; BP 10.39.31 shows weeping continuing until sunrise.

notes: No issues. Verse 21's 'kṣaṇa-bhaṅga-sauhṛdaḥ/nava-priyaḥ' is rendered per the standard lament reading.

statements.claim: At sunrise the gopis were still weeping; the night had been given to grief
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.31: 'strīṇām evaṃ rudantīnām udite savitary atha' (while the women wept thus the sun rose).

statements.claim: Nanda and the cowherds set out after the chariot with carts, the village stirring toward Mathura
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.32: 'gopās tam anvasajjanta nandādyāḥ śakaṭais tataḥ.'

statements.claim: The gopis followed Krishna on foot, their grief softened to near gladness by following him
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.33: 'gopyaś ca dayitaṃ kṛṣṇam anuvrajyānurañjitāḥ' (following their beloved Krishna, their hearts gladdened).

statements.claim: Krishna saw them grieving at his departure and sent them a message promising he would return
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.34 ('tās tathā tapyatīr vīkṣya sva-prasthāṇe yadūttamaḥ'); pack index excerpt: 'Krishna consoled them with messages, saying "I will come back"'. Note: the GRETIL verses 31-36 excerpted do not show the message's literal text; the pack's summary is treated as the intended reading.

statements.claim: The gopis followed while the banner and dust of the chariot remained visible, then lost hope and turned back toward Vraja
statements.evidence: BP 10.39.35-36: 'yāvad ālakṣyate ketur yāvad reṇū rathasya ca / tā nirāśā nivavṛtur govinda-vinivartane.'

statements.claim: Returning, they sang of his deeds, keeping his name alive until he should make good his word
statements.evidence: Pack index excerpt: 'and they returned, singing of his deeds' (rendered from 10.39.31-36).

notes: Pack summary explicitly includes the 'I will come back' message and the return singing; GRETIL verses 31-36 as excerpted are silent on the message text. Noted per instructions, treated as intended reading; no contradiction.

statements.claim: The vision in the river was withdrawn as an actor withdraws a play, and Akrura rose quickly from the Yamuna
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.1: 'so 'pi cāntarhitaṃ vīkṣya jalād unmajya satvaraḥ'; pack excerpt: 'Krishna withdrew the vision as an actor withdraws a play.'

statements.claim: Krishna asked Akrura what wonderful thing he had seen
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.2: 'tam apṛcchad dhṛṣīkeśaḥ kiṃ te dṛṣṭam ivādbhutam.'

statements.claim: Akrura answered that all wonders, on earth, in the sky or in water, stand in Krishna
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.4: 'yatrādbhutāni sarvāṇi bhūmau viyati vā jale.'

statements.claim: Wondering, Akrura urged the chariot on toward the city
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.5: 'ity uktvā codayām āsa syandanaṃ gāndinī-sutaḥ.'

statements.claim: On the road village people gathered to see them pass while the people of Vraja, Nanda and the cowherds, went ahead
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.6-7: 'mārge grāma-janā... tatra tatropasaṅgatāḥ / tāvad vrajaukasas tatra nanda-gopādayo 'grataḥ.'

statements.claim: Krishna told Akrura to enter the city first with his chariot and go to his own house
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.8-9: 'bhavān praviśatām agre saha-yānaḥ purīṃ gṛham.'

statements.claim: Akrura begged Krishna to come to his homes, make them not masterless, purify them with the dust of his feet; Bali became famous by washing those feet and the water purified the three worlds
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.11-14: 'āgaccha yāma gehān naḥ sa-nāthān kurv... punīhi pāda-rajasā... avanijyāṅghri-yugalam āsīt ślokyo balir mahān / āpas te 'ṅghry-avanejanyas trīṃl lokān śucayo 'punan.'

statements.claim: Akrura called Krishna god of gods whose name is auspicious to hear and sing, and asked him not to pass their doors
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.15: 'deva-deva jagan-nātha puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtana.'

statements.claim: In the afternoon Krishna entered Mathura with Balarama; Akrura, sent ahead, reported to Kamsa and then went to his own house, keeping the wonder privately
statements.evidence: BP 10.41.18: 'athāparāhṇe bhagavān kṛṣṇaḥ saṅkarṣaṇānvitaḥ'; pack excerpt: 'he entered Mathura, reported to Kamsa, and went to his own house.'

notes: No issues. The 'mirror' and 'source of all wonders' framing is connective narration consistent with the vision episode (DKS_0117).

statements.claim: Nanda and the men of Vraja had stayed in Mathura and now it was time to return home
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.19-24 context (Krishna bids Nanda return to Vraja); pack summary: 'Nanda... departed with the cowherds.'

statements.claim: Nanda and Yashoda had taken the child Krishna and his brother Balarama into their home and raised them as their own sons
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.21: 'sa pitā sā ca jananī yau puṣṇītāṃ sva-putra-vat' (he the father and she the mother who raised them like their own sons).

statements.claim: Krishna, son of Devaki, told Nanda and his wife that they nourished and cherished them with tenderness, brought up as their own sons
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.19-21: 'atha nandaṃ samasādya bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ / pitar yuvābhyāṃ snigdhābhyāṃ poṣitau lālitau bhṛśam / sa pitā sā ca jananī yau puṣṇītāṃ sva-putra-vat.'

statements.claim: Krishna bade Nanda go back to Vraja, saying they too were pained by affection, and promised to come and see his kinsfolk
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.22: 'yāta yūyaṃ vrajaṃ tāta vayaṃ ca sneha-duḥkhitān'; pack summary: 'promised to come and see his kinsfolk.'

statements.claim: Nanda, overwhelmed with affection, embraced Krishna and his brother, his eyes filled with tears, and departed with the cowherds
statements.evidence: BP 10.45.24: 'ity uktas tau pariṣvajya nandaḥ praṇaya-vihvalaḥ'; pack summary: 'Nanda, his eyes full of tears, departed with the cowherds.'

notes: No issues. 'Both homes were his now' is reflective connective narration.

statements.claim: Kamsa's champions fell one by one: Chanura and Toshala slain by Krishna; Mushtika and Andhra brought down by Balarama with thundercloud-like fists
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (Dutt): 'After Chānura... had been slain Rohini's son engaged with Mushthika and Krishna with Toshala again'; 'Taking up Toshala... Krishna grinded him on the earth'; 'fighting for a long time with Mushthika, and the wrestler Andhra... Baladeva struck his head with his fist resembling a cloud accompanied by a thunderbolt'; 'Having thus slain Toshala and Andhra, Krishna and Sangkarshana...'

statements.claim: Kamsa's face ran with sweat, the painted lines on his brow washed away in perspiration, his lips trembling with rage
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (60-63): 'drops of perspiration on Kansa's face... His lips trembling in anger and the painted lines on his forehead being washed off by perspiration.'

statements.claim: Kamsa ordered the two sinful, grim-faced forest cowherds turned out of the arena, saying he did not wish to see them and none of the cowherds deserved to remain in his territory
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (65-66): 'Turn out of the arena these two sinful, grim-visaged and forest-ranging young cow-herds. I do not wish to see them. Amongst the Gopas none deserves residence in my territory.'

statements.claim: Kamsa called Nanda wicked and bent on doing him harm, ordering him assailed with iron chains and spikes
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (67): 'This Nanda Gopa is wicked and is bent upon committing injury to me. Therefore assail him with iron chains and spikes.'

statements.claim: Kamsa called Vasudeva, his own kinsman, highly wicked and ordered him punished that very day in a way no aged man deserves
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (68): 'Although Vasudeva is my kinsman he is highly wicked. Therefore punish him even today in such a way which persons not, aged, deserve.'

statements.claim: Kamsa ordered the other cowherds, all devoted to Krishna, stripped of their cattle and wealth
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (69): 'The other inferior Gopas, whom you see, are all devoted to Krishna. Therefore take away from them their kine and other riches.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva fixed Kamsa with a long unblinking gaze; his strength was truth
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (70): 'Vāsudeva, having truth for his prowess, eyed him with eyes expanded in anger.'

statements.claim: Krishna saw Vasudeva and Nanda insulted, his kinsmen distressed and Devaki fallen senseless, and was greatly angered
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (71): 'Beholding his father Vasudeva and Nanda insulted, his kinsmen distressed and Devaki unconscious he was greatly worked up with anger.'

statements.claim: Krishna, with the speed of a lion, began to leap across the arena toward the king's pavilion to kill him
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (72-73): 'Desirous of ascending Kansa's pavillion in order to kill him, the powerful... Krishna, with the velocity of a lion, began to leap in the arena.'

statements.claim: Kamsa sat possessed by his own doom, unable to look plainly at Krishna
statements.evidence: HV 1.85 (75, 78): 'Kansa was completely possessed by Destiny... He was not capable of seeing even Krishna's face.'

notes: Pack passage file is truncated before the fight outcomes; verified against full HV 1.85 (same Dutt/Gutenberg #61937 source). All attributions match, including Devaki's fainting and the cattle-seizure order.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama ranged on the summit of Gomanta, wild-flower garlands on their chests, watching the sun and moon rise and set
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (1-4): 'began to range on the charming summit of Gomanta... Wearing on their breast garlands of wild flowers... see the sun and moon... at the time of the rising and setting of planets.'

statements.claim: Garuda, foremost of birds, had just returned from battle, body wounded by weapons, wearing celestial garlands, the crown blazing on his lap
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (37-38, 42): 'Vinatā's son, who had just returned from the battle-field, whose body was wounded with the strokes of weapons, who wore celestial garlands...'; 'While proceeding with that effulgent crown on his lap.'

statements.claim: Long ago, while Vishnu slept in the abode of Varuna in the ocean of milk, Virochana's son stole his crown, assuming a celestial form like the king of the gods
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (39, 48): 'When the Lord Vishnu was asleep in the abode of Varuna in the ocean of milk, Virochanana's son pilfered his crown'; 'Virochana's son, assuming a celestial form like that of the king of gods, stole away my diadem and took it away like a planet.'

statements.claim: Garuda fought a dreadful battle with the daityas in the ocean for the crown, won it, and not finding Vishnu passed over the earth toward the celestial regions
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (40-41): 'Garuda, the foremost of birds, fought a dreadful battle with the Daityas in that ocean, and securing it and not seeing Vishnu there, he was... passing through the surface of the earth, on his way to the celestial region.'

statements.claim: Garuda threw the crown from the welkin onto Krishna's head; it settled as if attached from before and shone like the midday sun on Mount Sumeru
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (43-45): 'threw from the welkin that crown on Vishnu's head in such a way as if it had been attached to his head from before. And placed upon Mādhava's head that diadem shone there like the mid-day sun on the summit of the mount Sumeru.'

statements.claim: Krishna said the work of the gods was near its fulfilment, that Virochana's son had stolen his crown while he slept in the ocean, and Garuda had brought it back
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (47-49): 'While arrangements for a battle have been completed on this mountain, methinks, the accomplishment of the work of gods is near at hand... When I fell asleep in the ocean... stole away my diadem... Garuda has brought this back.'

statements.claim: Krishna said Jarasandha was near — chariot-tops in sight, moon-white umbrellas and ordered armies moving like cranes — the first guest in battle, a touchstone for their strength
statements.evidence: HV 1.97 (50-55): 'I think it for certain that Jarāsandha is near at hand, for the tops of the cars... are being seen now... moon-like umbrellas and well-arranged armies... coming towards us like cranes in the sky... He is our first guest in battle and is like a touch-stone for testing our military skill.'

notes: Pack passage file is truncated mid-chapter (Balarama/drinking portion); the Garuda-crown and Jarasandha content verified against full HV 1.97 (same source). The story omits the Varuni/Kadamvari interlude, which precedes the crown episode; no contradiction.

statements.claim: The two sons of Vasudeva traveled five nights in the company of Damaghosha, keeping the ways of a traveler
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (1): 'The two heroic sons of Vasudeva, united with Damaghosha, spent five nights with delight like one in the way according to the rules of a traveller.'

statements.claim: Ugrasena came out first at the head of the Yadavas; traders, subjects, ministers, boys and old men all came out to receive them
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (3-4): 'all the Yadavas, headed by Ugrasena, came out to receive them... All the traders, subjects, ministers and the boys and old men of Mathurā came out.'

statements.claim: The city was dressed as for a festival: garlands and flags at the crossings of four streets, joyful trumpets, panegyrists singing their glories; Mathura looked as on the day of Indra's festival
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (5-6): 'All the crossings of four streets were decorated with garlands and flags; trumpets were beaten announcing joy and panegyrists began to sing the glories... beautiful as on the occasion of an Indrayajna.'

statements.claim: Singers announced along the highways that the brothers Rama and Govinda, celebrated in the world, had arrived at their own city
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (7-8): 'the two brothers Rāma and Govinda, celebrated in the world, have arrived at their own city.'

statements.claim: Where Rama and Krishna passed no one was poor, in soiled clothes or unconscious; cows, horses and elephants grew glad; birds sounded auspicious notes; clean winds blew from the ten directions; temple images brightened; all signs of the Krita (golden) age appeared
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (9-12): 'none in the city of Mathurā was poorly, in dirty clothes and unconscious. Cows, horses and elephants grew delightful and birds began to emit auspicious notes... Auspicious winds, shorn of dust, began to blow in the ten quarters and all the images of deities in temples were delighted. All the signs of the Krita age appeared there in Mathurā.'

statements.claim: Seated on a chariot drawn by fine horses, at an auspicious moment, Rama and Krishna entered the city; the Yadavas followed as the gods follow Indra
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (13-14): 'seated on a car drawn by beautiful horses Rāma and Keshava entered the city of Mathurā in an auspicious moment. As the gods follow Shakra the Yādavas followed Rāma and Govinda.'

statements.claim: The brothers entered the house of their father Vasudeva like the sun and moon entering a mountain, set aside their weapons of their own accord
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (15-16): 'As the sun and moon enter into the mountain so those two... entered into the house of their sire Vasudeva. Keeping their respective weapons there of their own accord.'

statements.claim: They bowed to Vasudeva's feet, showed honor to king Ugrasena and the leading Yadavas, and were welcomed in return before entering their mother's apartments
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (17-18): 'bowing unto the feet of Vasudeva they showed proper honor to king Ugrasena and other leading Yadavas... They, too, welcomed by them duly in return, delightedly entered into their mother's appartment.'

statements.claim: In the days that followed they stayed close to Ugrasena and lived in Mathura happily
statements.evidence: HV 1.101 (19): 'following Ugrasena, Rāma and Keshava... spent some days happily in Mathurā.'
